name: Mauritius
summary: An Indian Ocean island ruled by the Dutch, French and British, with no people before them; sugar plantations brought enslaved Africans and Indian workers. Independent in 1968, it became one of Africa’s richest democracies.

knownFor.label: Sega
knownFor.note: Music and dance of enslaved Africans.

location.value: Indian Ocean east of Madagascar; about 2,040 km².

terrain.value: Volcanic island with a central plateau, ringed by reefs.

climate.value: Tropical, with a hot, wet summer (November–April), a cooler dry winter and risk of cyclones.

resources.value: Fertile soil for sugar cane, fish, and beautiful beaches for tourism.

disasters.value: Cyclones (storms) strike regularly, and rising sea levels threaten the coast.

population.value: About 1.3 million people in the early 2020s.

urbanisation.value: Most people live in and around the capital.

disease.value: Good basic health care; rising diabetes.

economicBase.value: Tourism, textiles, financial services and sugar, a shift from sugar alone in the 1970s.

tradeRoutes.value: Shipping through Port Louis, and flights, link the island to India, Africa, Europe and Asia.

wealth.value: An upper-middle-income country, among the richest in Africa per person.

moneyAndTax.value: The Mauritian rupee, with a low flat tax rate to attract investment.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A parliamentary democracy within the Commonwealth, a republic since 1992.

keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Mauritius (checked 8 Nov 2026); Britannica: Mauritius independence (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Britannica does not name the first prime minister; it says Anerood Jugnauth was prime minister in 1982–95 and 2000–03)

succession.value: Elections to the National Assembly choose a prime minister, who is the head of government.

stability.value: A stable multi-party democracy with peaceful changes of government.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between parties and family dynasties.

armyAndTech.value: No army: a police force with a small special force and a coast guard.

majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Mauritius; Britannica: Mauritius independence (checked 15 Nov 2026) (the page describes no war; the first real domestic disturbances were riots in 1999, and coast guard commandos were deployed against piracy in 2010–13)

territoryChange.value: The state includes Rodrigues and outlying islands; sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago has long been disputed with the United Kingdom.

alliancesRivals.value: Britain split the Chagos Archipelago from Mauritius in 1965; after the International Court of Justice ordered its return, a bilateral agreement recognising Mauritian sovereignty was signed in May 2025.

inventions.value: No major inventions; the island is known for its mix of cultures and sugar-industry history.

scienceEducation.value: Free schooling and the University of Mauritius (founded 1965).

openness.value: An open, export-led economy that trades widely and welcomes foreign investment.

communicationTransport.value: Ferries and flights link Mauritius with Rodrigues and Réunion; a light-rail metro opened in 2020.

religion.value: Hinduism is the largest religion (about 48%), followed by Christianity (about 32%) and Islam (about 18%) (2022 census).

artsArchitecture.value: Hindu temples, mosques, churches and French colonial plantation houses, plus sega music.

sharedIdentity.value: A shared island identity built from Indian, African, Chinese and European roots, with Creole as a common spoken language.

dailyLife.value: Families eat curries and dholl puri, and festivals such as Diwali and Eid are public holidays.

ideasReligions.value: Hinduism, Christianity, Islam and Buddhism live side by side, and religious tolerance is a source of pride.

riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Mauritius (checked 8 Nov 2026); Britannica: Mauritius independence (checked 15 Nov 2026) (independent within the Commonwealth on 12 March 1968, with a governor-general; it became a republic on 12 March 1992)

peakPeriod.value: The “Mauritian miracle”, fast growth from the 1980s that raised incomes.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Mauritius continues as an independent state.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
